title: skyBlip companion link registry (v1)
description: Every frame on the companion link's config, log and peer endpoints, and the number each of its keys travels under. A frame is one CBOR map (RFC 8949) in one write or one notification, in one grammar every reader of the link holds to: the map's keys unsigned and ascending, every head in its shortest form and its argument within 32 bits, definite lengths only, no floats, no tags, no null, and nothing nested but an array of unsigned integers. Text is UTF-8: the firmware writes nothing else and every reader refuses a malformed sequence. link.v1.vectors.json holds what the readers refuse and what the clients' encoders refuse, and the firmware, blip.py and the server each test against it. Key 0 is 'command' in every frame and is not listed under 'keys': its value is the 'code' of a frame below, which says which frame this is and therefore which key table applies. A frame's 'keys' list every other key it may carry, each with its 'name' (what a client shows and accepts), its 'number', assigned once and never reused within the frame, and its 'type': 'unsigned' and 'integer' (a CBOR unsigned or negative integer; 'unsigned' is never negative), 'boolean', 'text' (UTF-8, only for free text a person reads or types), 'bytes' (a byte string, never hex or base64; 'bytes' with a number is its fixed length), 'unsigned_array' (an array of unsigned integers) and 'enum' (an unsigned integer whose names are the values of the enum named by 'enum'). Every frame and every key has a 'description': what it means, when it is present and the range it takes. A key with 'required' true is in every frame of its command that carries keys: the unit's answer where the host asks with the bare command, the host's own frame where only the host sends one. A frame with 'keys_of' shares the key table of the frame it names, so the same key is the same number in both: 'set', 'config' and 'defaults' are one table, so a 'defaults' reply with its command swapped is a 'set', and 'radio' is the radio group of 'diagnostics'. 'endpoint' is the characteristic it travels on, 'sender' who writes it: 'host' (a page, blip.py), 'unit', or 'both' when the host asks with the bare command and the unit answers under the same one. On the peer endpoint the unit is a skyBlip Bravo and the host the skyBlip Go paired with it (firmware/core/comms/README.md, The peer endpoint). Under 'enums', each value has a 'name' and a 'code'; 'mirrors' names the C++ enum whose numbering the codes are and, under 'off_the_wire', the enumerators the link never carries, and a value's 'mirrors' its enumerator. firmware/test/core/test_link_mirrors.cpp holds them to it both ways: each code to its enumerator, and the enum to the registry through a switch over every value named here, which -Wswitch refuses to compile once the C++ enum gains one the registry lacks. firmware/core/comms/README.md says how the link carries them, and schemas/activation.v1.schema.json what the activation signatures cover and the JSON the browser posts to the server. scripts/link_registry.py generates firmware/core/comms/link_registry.h, firmware/simulator/world/link_names.h, firmware/test/core/test_link_mirrors.cpp and server/app/javascript/skyblip/link_registry.js from this file, and scripts/check_link_registry.py fails when one of them differs from what it would write, when a frame or a key has no description, and when firmware/core/comms/config_reports.cpp writes the status frame other than its keys say. firmware/test/products/test_link_registry.cpp drives the product through every command of the config and log endpoints and holds every frame the unit sends to this file, its keys, their types, byte widths and codes, and the required ones present, and holds the unit to reading every key a host frame lists. firmware/test/products/test_peer_frames.cpp pins the peer frames byte for byte at their widest. A unit refuses as invalid a command carrying a key its frame does not list, or any key at all on a bare ask. scripts/blip_frames.py, which scripts/blip.py speaks through, reads this file directly.

frames.description: Unit to host on the config endpoint: the verdict on a command that has no reply of its own, the refusal of any config command, and a prompt standing on the glass and its verdict, a log erase's included. 11 bytes at its widest, so every link carries it.

keys.name: acknowledge
keys.description: The command was carried out. False is a refusal, or a prompt waiting on the glass when pending is true

keys.name: pending
keys.description: Present only as true: a prompt stands on the glass under the word in reason. Two presses answer it with the command's verdict, one press answers cancelled, thirty seconds expired and a take-off in_flight, and the asking link dropping takes it without an answer. No command renews it: the thirty seconds run from the staging, and a command that would stage another prompt while it stands is refused prompt_pending. After one press answers cancelled, every command from that link that would stage a prompt is refused refused_on_device until the link drops

keys.name: reason
keys.description: The word for the verdict, the refusal or the prompt, from the one enumeration every frame shares (firmware/core/comms/README.md and server/app/javascript/skyblip/README.md say which command answers which). Absent only on the verdict of a set the presses stored

keys.name: by
keys.description: On a claimed refusal, the link session id of the central that holds the claim: one central at a time commands the unit (firmware/core/comms/README.md, The claim)

frames.description: Host to unit, a bare ask for the stored settings, answered by a config frame.

Unit to host, the answer to get: the stored settings a host may change, the settings contract's version, and the unit's address and its mapping table, in one frame of at most 37 bytes. config, set and defaults share this key table, and so do the Go and Bravo: each key says which product stores it, and Bravo answers config with its own keys and ignores the rest of a set (#176). The two per-unit trims, battery_offset_mv and frequency_trim_e1_ppm, are written by a host and never returned. The radar's range and plot are stored settings with no key here: they are set on the device's own menu. address is absent until the unit is activated, and every other key but the trims is always present, own_icao as 0 while it is unset.

keys.name: version
keys.description: The settings contract, 1 (products/skyblip_go/settings.h, kCurrentVersion): it moves when a key changes meaning, not when the flash layout does. Always in config, never in defaults, and ignored in a set. Sent by the Go

keys.name: address
keys.description: The 24-bit ADS-L address this unit transmits under: the manufacturer prefix 0x00 followed by the 16-bit serial skyblip.eu signed at activation (schemas/activation.v1.schema.json). Absent until the unit is activated, so a page reads its presence as activated. Read-only: the unit re-verifies its unlock code at every boot, and a set carrying it is ignored. Sent by the Go only: Bravo has no ADS-L address (#184)

keys.name: address_mapping_table
keys.description: ADS-L address mapping table (issue 2 F.2.2), 0 to 63: 0=random/privacy, 1-4 reserved, 5=ICAO, 6=FLARM, 7=OGN-Tracker, 8=FANET, 9+ manufacturer pages, each a registry-assigned 8-bit prefix and a 16-bit base address. A constant 58 on this device, manufacturer page 49 with prefix 0x00 as the ADS-L registry assigned it, so address is that prefix and the unit's serial. Present whether or not the unit is activated. Read-only: a set carrying it is ignored. Sent by the Go only

keys.name: aircraft_type
keys.description: ADS-L aircraft category, 0 to 17. A set past 17 is refused out_of_range. Stored by the Go

keys.name: alarm_enabled
keys.description: The traffic alarm sounds. False silences the buzzer and the haptic both, as alarm_volume off does. Stored by the Go and by Bravo

keys.name: alarm_volume
keys.description: The three steps of the radar menu's VOLUME row. off silences the buzzer and the haptic both, as alarm_enabled false does. soft and loud set the buzzer's loudness, and the haptic pulses with each call at either. A device ships on loud. Stored by the Go and by Bravo

keys.name: units
keys.description: nautical (nautical miles, knots) or metric (kilometres, km/h): what every distance and speed on the glass is printed in, the radar's range ring, the nearby page's distance column and the six-pack's speed dial. Altitudes and vertical speeds stay in feet whatever this says. A device ships on nautical. Stored by the Go

keys.name: callsign
keys.description: The aircraft's registration as the radio says it: up to nine characters of A to Z, 0 to 9, dash and blank, the ones the radar menu types. A set with any other character is refused invalid, and a longer one out_of_range. Empty, the default, transmits no name, so an address a receiver cannot resolve stays anonymous. Otherwise the unit transmits it once every ten seconds under ADS-L payload 66 (core/timing/README.md). Stored by the Go

keys.name: battery_offset_mv
keys.description: From -250 to 250, past which a set is refused out_of_range. The per-unit battery gauge trim in millivolts, added to every reading before a state of charge or a cutoff is read from it, and set once on the production line against a bench supply (core/power/battery.h says why the bound is 250). Written by a host only: config and defaults never carry it. Stored by the Go

keys.name: frequency_trim_e1_ppm
keys.description: From -100 to 100, past which a set is refused out_of_range. The radio's centre-frequency trim in tenths of a ppm, positive upwards, applied to every dwell the SX1262 arms. The board fits a TCXO, so 0 is the design intent: the trim answers a batch of references far outside their datasheet, and is set only against a spectrum analyser or a frequency counter. Inside the bound the carrier stays inside ERC 70-03 band h1.4 (868.0 to 868.6 MHz). Written by a host only: config and defaults never carry it. Stored by the Go

keys.name: own_icao
keys.description: The 24-bit ICAO address of the aircraft's own Mode-S transponder, 0 to 16777215, past which a set is refused out_of_range. 0, the default, is unset, and a set of 0 clears it, which the glass confirms as it confirms every set. The traffic table refuses this address under table 5, so the aircraft's own transponder is not traffic (firmware/core/traffic/README.md). It is the aircraft's address and not the unit's: address is what the unit transmits under, and this key does not change it. Always in config and defaults. Stored by the Go and by Bravo

frames.description: Host to unit, a bare ask, answered under defaults with the settings a pilot can set as a new unit ships them: aircraft_type, alarm_enabled, alarm_volume, units, callsign and own_icao, so the reply with its command swapped for set puts a unit back on its defaults. version, the address keys, the per-unit trims and the radar's range and plot are not in it.

Host to unit: the keys of config to change, all or none. A value out of range is refused out_of_range, a wrong type or a callsign the menu cannot type invalid, and nothing is stored. version, address and address_mapping_table are read-only and ignored. Refused low_power while the cell is below the settings write rule, and in_flight while the unit is airborne. A take-off cancels a staged set. Otherwise the unit asks on its glass under confirm, and two presses store the change and answer an acknowledgement with no reason. A trusted browser (trust_browser) is not asked: the change is stored at once and answered the same way, in flight too. While a prompt stands it is refused prompt_pending, and after one press refused a prompt on this link refused_on_device, until the link drops (firmware/core/comms/README.md, One prompt at a time).

Asked with the bare command, and the one frame the unit also sends without being asked: while a link is up, a change of flight state, a charging flip, a change of power level, a five-percent step of the state of charge or a change of bravo pushes it to every subscribed central. With every key at its widest it is 22 bytes, pinned byte for byte in firmware/test/products/test_comms_report.cpp, and 20 on a unit that is not paired with a Bravo, the payload every link guarantees. A status over 20 bytes, usual for a paired Go in flight, is dropped on a link that stayed at 20 bytes: a push silently, an ask with small_mtu. It carries what a pilot's screen shows and nothing a bench reads: why the device came up is reset and whether a gauge is fitted is battery_valid in diagnostics, the address and the callsign are config's. A key with no reading behind it is absent, never a zero. The firmware writes the keys in ascending number, and scripts/check_link_registry.py holds firmware/core/comms/config_reports.cpp to this table: the keys, their order, their types and which may be absent.

keys.name: flight
keys.description: The confirmed flight state. A firmware install, a recovery, a power-off, a cold start, a log request, a set and an activated unit's activation are refused while this reads airborne, and go ahead on ground and on unknown, a unit with no fix since boot

keys.name: upload
keys.description: A firmware upload window is open and the unit is not airborne: two presses after dfu open it for ten minutes, and a take-off, one press, the claim holder's link dropping or the upload landing closes it

keys.name: battery_percent
keys.description: 0 to 100, the state of charge read on the discharge curve, 0 at 3200 mV, where the unit takes itself down. Absent until the gauge has a reading of the cell: for ever on a board with no divider, and while the cable is in, because the divider reads the USB rail there

keys.name: charging
keys.description: The cable is in. No pin says when the charge ends, so a full cell on the cable still reads true

keys.name: power_level
keys.description: What core/power's cutoff rule made of the cell: low below 3600 mV, critical below 3500 mV and flat below 3200 mV, each entered after three consecutive readings below it and left after three back above it by 35 mV (core/power/cutoff.h). low asks for a charger, critical refuses every settings write, flat is the unit taking itself down, and unknown is no believable reading yet. The glass and the USB console print OK, LOW, CRITICAL, FLAT and --

keys.name: went_dark_flat
keys.description: The last time this unit went dark it was for a flat cell: the cutoff took it down, or a switch-on was refused below the boot lockout. The glass says FLAT BATTERY until a charger wakes the unit, and this outlives that frame: true for the whole of the one boot that followed, false from the boot after. The self-test page prints the same fact as WAS FLAT

keys.name: die_temperature_c
keys.description: Die temperature in whole degrees Celsius, rounded away from zero. Absent rather than zero when no reading younger than 30 seconds exists, because 0 C is a plausible hangar morning. The same value as diagnostics' die_temperature_c

keys.name: bravo
keys.description: What a Go paired with a Bravo makes of its Bravo's health frames (firmware/core/comms/README.md, What the Go makes of its Bravo): live, waiting until the first health of the boot or until the pinned Bravo first has UTC since the Go booted or paired, or why it is lost, link_down, receiver_down or no_utc, which the glass shows as BRAVO LOST. Absent on a unit that is not paired

frames.description: The bench's slot timing report, asked with the bare command (core/timing/slot_timing_statistics.h): the PPS and dwell histograms and the executor's switching figures, since boot. One frame on a 182-byte link, 147 bytes at its widest, and consecutive parts on a narrower one. Refused no_statistics where no accumulator is wired, and small_mtu on a link too narrow for one histogram.

keys.name: part
keys.description: Frame index within one answer, from 0

keys.name: more
keys.description: Another frame follows. Exactly one frame per answer carries false

keys.name: pps_us
keys.description: Counts of PPS interval errors in seven buckets, signed and symmetric about zero, edged at kRetuneUs (30 us), kHopGuardUs and kJitterGuardUs (core/timing/slot_timing_statistics.h). An error past the widest edge lands in the outermost bucket

keys.name: pps_worst_us
keys.description: The PPS interval error of the largest magnitude since boot, signed, in microseconds

keys.name: pps_samples
keys.description: PPS intervals counted in pps_us

keys.name: dwell_us
keys.description: Counts of dwell phase errors, from the armed instant to the burst keying, in the seven buckets of pps_us

keys.name: dwell_worst_us
keys.description: The dwell phase error of the largest magnitude since boot, signed, in microseconds

keys.name: dwell_samples
keys.description: Dwell phases counted in dwell_us

keys.name: holdover_events
keys.description: Times the PPS stream broke since boot: a lost lock, or two edges more than 1.5 s apart or out of order. Such an interval is not a sample for pps_us

keys.name: missed
keys.description: Dwells that carried a plan and closed without the outcome they were armed for

keys.name: refused
keys.description: Plans never armed because the hour's air-time budget was spent (core/timing/transmit.h)

keys.name: switch_hop_us
keys.description: The executor's slowest M-band channel hop since boot, in microseconds, the figure the hop guard is sized from

keys.name: switch_to_o_band_us
keys.description: The executor's slowest change from the M band to the O band since boot, in microseconds

keys.name: switch_to_m_band_us
keys.description: The executor's slowest change from the O band back to the M band since boot, in microseconds

keys.name: late_dwells
keys.description: Dwells armed ahead that were still not listening at their start

frames.description: The durable-write window's bench figures, asked with the bare command (core/timing/durable_write.h): how the settings writes were placed against the radio's dwells since boot. Refused no_statistics where no window is wired.

keys.name: writable
keys.description: The power rule allows a settings write now (core/power/cutoff.h)

keys.name: requests
keys.description: Changes that asked for a durable write since boot

keys.name: writes
keys.description: Writes those changes cost: requests over writes is the coalescing ratio

keys.name: forced
keys.description: Writes that could not be placed outside a dwell inside the bound and were forced

keys.name: worst_wait_ms
keys.description: The longest a change waited for its write, from the oldest unwritten change

keys.name: pending
keys.description: A change is waiting for its write now

keys.name: budget_ms
keys.description: kWorstWriteMs, the longest one settings write may take, which a placed write keeps clear of the next dwell

keys.name: bound_ms
keys.description: kDeferCeilingMs, the longest a change may wait before its write is forced

frames.description: Asked with the bare command: the radio group of diagnostics alone, answered under radio with the keys of diagnostics. Unlike the whole dump it is answered before a dump has been collected, since a radio that has heard nothing truthfully has zero receptions.

One dump, two surfaces, one table behind both (firmware/core/comms/diagnostics.h). Asked with the bare command and answered as one frame per subsystem, or more where the negotiated payload cannot carry a subsystem whole: every frame carries group, part and more, no frame mixes two groups, and no frame exceeds the payload the asking central negotiated. To a USB host that raised DTR the same table is printed every ten seconds, one line per subsystem, '<group> key=value key="text value" ...', with the same group names, keys and values, an enumeration printed as the words the glass uses (reset="CPU LOCKUP" where the link carries lockup). Asking before the device has collected a dump is refused no_statistics, since a device must not report health it has not measured. Nothing here is reset by being read. Each key's description starts with the group it belongs to. The widest group, the adsb group, is 127 bytes, and the radio's 112. Key 53, the adsb group's invalid, is retired and never reused: crc and unsupported split it.

keys.name: group
keys.description: The subsystem every field in this frame belongs to. One console line per group, in this order.

keys.name: part
keys.description: Frame index within one answer, from 0. A group that does not fit the negotiated payload spans consecutive parts

keys.name: more
keys.description: Another frame follows. Exactly one frame per answer carries false

keys.name: uptime_s
keys.description: system. Seconds since boot, the pass's 32-bit millisecond clock over 1000, so it wraps at 49.7 days

keys.name: reset
keys.description: system. Why the device came up (core/power/reset_reason.h). The console prints the words core/power/reset_reason.cpp spells: UNKNOWN, POWER ON, RESET PIN, BROWNOUT, SOFT RESET, WATCHDOG, CPU LOCKUP, CHARGER WAKE, BUTTON WAKE, DEBUGGER

keys.name: link_drops
keys.description: system. Config endpoint frames the unit could not send: wider than the asking link's payload, refused by the controller, or left incomplete by a writer. The log endpoint counts its own, which are not in this

keys.name: noise_dbm
keys.description: radio. The measured noise floor, core/timing::NoiseFloor, in dBm, from -128 to 127. A diagnostic and nothing else: nothing on this device defers a burst to what it hears, so a loud site is reported rather than transmitted around (firmware/core/timing/README.md)

keys.name: duty_permille
keys.description: radio. Parts per thousand, 0 to 1000, of the transmit allowance spent over the hour's sliding window (EN 300 220-2 V3.3.1 Table 4 band M, 1%). The declared channel-access route, and the only rule that refuses a burst

keys.name: rx_ok
keys.description: radio. Frames received and decoded

keys.name: rx_bad
keys.description: radio. Receptions that are a fault: a frame that framed, was attempted and was refused, plus the integrity failures an error correction could not rescue. Not a burst nothing was attempted on (rx_wait), not a message type this firmware does not implement (rx_type), not a burst that named no system at all (rx_unframed), not a frame keyed on a second we disagree with (rx_miskeyed), and not a transmission of ours that never completed (tx_lost)

keys.name: rx_wait
keys.description: radio. Frames no decode was attempted on, because an ALP-TAS position is coded relative to the receiver and keyed on the UTC second, so it needs a fix and a date of our own. Climbs on a device still acquiring next to a transmitting neighbour, which is correct behaviour and not a failure

keys.name: rx_type
keys.description: radio. Frames that framed and carried a message type this firmware does not implement: ALP-TAS reads its 2024 position frame and nothing else, so a SoftRF interleaving Air V6 with Air V7 lands here. The neighbour's dialect, not our failure

keys.name: rx_unframed
keys.description: radio. Bursts that held the shared sync window and decoded too cleanly to be noise, but whose sync tail named neither M-band system. A neighbour on another dialect, or a receiver framing at the wrong offset: either way not a frame this firmware refused

keys.name: rx_miskeyed
keys.description: radio. ALP-TAS frames whose CRC held and whose sender keyed them on a second inside 18 s of ours but not ours: the key stage moves every 16 s and the frame carries the low 4 bits of its own second, so a clock disagreement is reported as the offset it is rather than as a decode failure. Climbing here means one of the two clocks is wrong, not the radio

keys.name: rx_noise
keys.description: radio. What the band's own noise framed: a sync window that filled with something carrying no frame at all. The floor under every other reception counter, and the one that tells a deaf receiver from an empty sky

keys.name: rx_named
keys.description: radio. Bursts that framed and carried an aircraft's registration instead of its position: ADS-L payload 66, OGN's, read for the callsign and filed under the sender's address (core/radio/README.md, radio::Verdict::Named). Counted apart from rx_ok, which counts positions

keys.name: tx_ok
keys.description: radio. Bursts the executor reported as transmitted

keys.name: tx_lost
keys.description: radio. Bursts of ours that were armed and never completed: the dwell ran out, or the radio's transmit timeout did. Never a reception

keys.name: tx_named
keys.description: radio. How many of the bursts in tx_ok carried own-ship's registration rather than a position: the callsign goes on the air once every ten seconds, in slot 1's tail (core/timing/README.md)

keys.name: tx_keyed_us
keys.description: radio. Microseconds the last burst held the carrier keyed, measured by the executor rather than budgeted

keys.name: tx_span_us
keys.description: radio. Microseconds from arming the last burst to the radio reporting it sent, which is the keyed time plus everything around it

keys.name: range_refused
keys.description: radio. Receptions core/traffic refused because the position they claimed was further away than this radio can hear (core/traffic/sanity.h). A rate that climbs is a receiver at the edge of its link budget or a decoder that is silently miscorrecting

keys.name: dio1_armed
keys.description: radio. The executor holds a rising-edge interrupt on the SX1262's DIO1 and sleeps on it between events. False on the host executor, which has no interrupt line, and on silicon when the GPIO driver refused the trigger: the executor then reads DIO1 every 200 us instead

keys.name: dio1_edges
keys.description: radio. DIO1 rising edges the interrupt handler saw since boot. Near rx and tx events combined on a healthy line; zero with dio1_armed true is a trigger that never fires

keys.name: dio1_missed
keys.description: radio. Events a status read found while DIO1 still read low: a TxDone read in the tail of a burst, the 4 ms safety poll, or the drain at a dwell's end. Rising with tx_ok means DIO1 trails TxDone, rising with rx_ok means it trails RxDone too

keys.name: tracked
keys.description: traffic. Aircraft currently in the table, after ageing out, at most 48

keys.name: alarm
keys.description: traffic. The alarm level standing now: 0 none, 1 advisory (core/traffic/alarm.h)

keys.name: fixes
keys.description: gnss. Solutions own-ship took from the receiver since boot, with a fix or without. Zero on a device whose receiver is wired but silent

keys.name: valid
keys.description: gnss. Whether own-ship currently holds a valid fix

keys.name: baud
keys.description: gnss. The rate the unit talks to the receiver at: the devicetree's rate until autobaud had to move. A receiver silently at another rate is a GNSS-less device that looks fitted

keys.name: config
keys.description: gnss. Where the receiver's configuration sequence stands (ports::GnssConfigStage, run by hardware/parts/l76k): idle before it starts, restarting, waking, identifying by the $PCAS06 banner, sending the $PCAS sentences, verifying that the receiver obeys them, confirming while a raised port rate waits for its first sentence, then ready; degraded once three verifications failed with no other rate left to try. The console prints IDLE, RESTART, WAKING, IDENT, SENDING, VERIFY, CONFIRM, READY and DEGRADED

keys.name: raises
keys.description: gnss. Times the driver asked the receiver to move to 115200 baud with $PCAS01, which it does only after the receiver passed verification and only on a port that can retune (core/gnss/README.md)

keys.name: raise_fallbacks
keys.description: gnss. Raises after which no sentence checksummed at the new rate inside the 3 s verify window, so the port went back to the rate before: a receiver that ignored $PCAS01, which never acknowledges

keys.name: solution_phase_ms
keys.description: gnss. Milliseconds after the latched PPS edge at which own-ship last published a solution, modulo 1000 (products/common/services/ownship.cpp). A solution that lands past the 450 ms direct slot start is read as a second old and its burst refused (core/gnss/README.md). Absent while PPS is not locked

keys.name: overruns
keys.description: gnss. Times the UART interrupt read bytes from the receiver that its receive ring had no room for, and dropped them (hardware/platform/zephyr/io.h): a service pass that stalled longer than the ring holds at the port's rate

keys.name: identified
keys.description: gnss. The receiver answered the $PCAS06 handshake and named itself. False means an unidentified part, still configured, but a $PCAS dialect we cannot confirm

keys.name: firmware
keys.description: gnss. The receiver's own firmware banner, at most 23 characters of printable ASCII, e.g. URANUS5,V5.1.0.0. Empty when it never introduced itself

keys.name: reject
keys.description: gnss. Why the last solution was not accepted as a fix (core/gnss/validity.h), none when it was

keys.name: rejected
keys.description: gnss. Solutions refused since boot, one event per run of the same reason

keys.name: residual_m
keys.description: gnss. The extrapolation residual in metres, saturating at 65535: the model the transmitter applies, run over the interval that just elapsed and measured against the fix that closed it. Absent rather than zero when there is no pair of consecutive fixes to measure, because 0 m is what a perfect prediction reports

keys.name: cell_mv
keys.description: power. The battery reading in millivolts, after the per-unit trim (settings.battery_offset_mv): the cell when battery_valid, otherwise what the divider last read, 0 when the ADC gave nothing.

keys.name: percent
keys.description: power. State of charge from the same reading, on the discharge curve, 0 to 100. 0 unless battery_valid

keys.name: battery_valid
keys.description: power. Whether cell_mv is the cell. False with no divider, on a reading outside 1800 to 4700 mV, and on the cable, where the divider reads the USB rail.

keys.name: charging
keys.description: power. The cable is in. No pin says when the charge ends, so a full cell on the cable still reads true

keys.name: power_level
keys.description: power. The status reply's power_level, from the same samples. The console prints OK, LOW, CRITICAL, FLAT and --

keys.name: supply_warnings
keys.description: power. Times the nRF52840's power-failure comparator (POFCON) has fired. Any at all on a healthy cell is a supply problem or a threshold set too high, and both are bench work

keys.name: implausible
keys.description: power. Readings the gauge refused: at or under 1800 mV, an unpopulated or unconnected divider rather than a flat cell, or over 4700 mV, which no 4.2 V cell reaches and a rail does. On the cable or off it. cell_mv holds the last one while battery_valid is false

keys.name: die_temperature_c
keys.description: power. Die temperature in whole degrees Celsius, rounded away from zero. Absent rather than zero when no reading younger than 30 seconds exists. The same value as the status reply's

keys.name: charge
keys.description: power. Whether the die temperature allows the cell to charge (core/power/charging.h): too_cold under 5.0 C, too_hot over 60.0 C, ok between, against LilyGO's 0 to 60 C window with the die's own warmth as the margin at the cold end. Judged only on the cable with a die reading and absent otherwise, so unknown never travels. The console prints OK, COLD and HOT

keys.name: charge_warnings
keys.description: power. Times the charge condition changed into too_cold or too_hot (products/common/services/power.cpp): a cable left in a cold cockpit is one warning, not one a pass

keys.name: frames
keys.description: adsb. 1090 MHz frames the LR2021 handed up since boot: each is a preamble and a 0x95 sync with 27 chips behind it, valid or not (hardware/parts/lr2021). The adsb group is sent only by a unit with a 1090 MHz receiver

keys.name: frame_rate_hz
keys.description: adsb. Frames handed up over the last whole second, 0 after a silent one

keys.name: dropped
keys.description: adsb. Frames lost before the decoder: the queue to it was full (core/events/adsb.h sizes it), or the LR2021's FIFO overflowed, which counts every frame the FIFO held, since the driver clears it and starts receive again

keys.name: rearms
keys.description: adsb. Times the receiver went back into receive through standby after 30 s without a frame (runtime::kRadioRxSilenceCeilingMs). Climbs once every 30 s under an empty sky

keys.name: resets
keys.description: adsb. Times the LR2021 was reset and brought up again, after BUSY stayed high past its ceiling or a re-arm failed

keys.name: command_errors
keys.description: adsb. Commands the LR2021 answered CMD_FAIL or CMD_PERR in the status that opens the next frame (LR20xx datasheet Rev. 2.1, 6.7.1)

keys.name: errors
keys.description: adsb. The LR2021's GetErrors word at the end of its last bring-up (LR20xx datasheet Rev. 2.1, 6.7.4). Bit 0, HF_XOSC_START_ERR, and bit 2, PLL_LOCK_ERR, refuse the bring-up. The others are kept for the bench, since 1090 MHz is past the 960 MHz the LF path is specified to

keys.name: rssi_dbm
keys.description: adsb. Counts of frames by the level of their pulses (RssiHigh), in eight buckets whose floors are -128, -90, -80, -70, -60, -50, -40 and -30 dBm (ports/adsb_receiver.h). A frame read in the same wake as a newer one has no level of its own, and neither has the newest when the two packet-status reads around the FIFO level disagree: those are in frames only

keys.name: crc
keys.description: adsb. Frames core/protocol's adsb_receive refused on parity: the CRC failed, and the one repair it allows, a single doubtful chip pair, did not clear it. A weak or damaged frame, or a DF16, whose parity carries an address. A development image prints these frames on its console with their chips, as it does the unsupported ones (firmware/products/skyblip_bravo/README.md, Reading the rejects)

keys.name: unsupported
keys.description: adsb. Frames whose parity held but whose message the decoder does not read: a DF17 of type code 0 or 23 to 30, of type 19 with a subtype other than 1 to 4, or of type 31 with a subtype past 1 (core/protocol/adsb.cpp). Sound receptions, not damage

keys.name: folded
keys.description: adsb. Messages protocol::AdsbAssembly folded into an aircraft since boot: a position, a velocity, an identification or an operational status. A message from the own ICAO is not counted, nor one from a new aircraft refused because the 100 the assembly holds all matter more

keys.name: aircraft
keys.description: adsb. Aircraft protocol::AdsbAssembly holds now, at most 100: each heard inside the last 250 s, with or without a position, before the traffic table. tracked, in the traffic group, counts the ones the table took

frames.description: The image's state and what an install needs: asked with the bare command, and pushed to a connection when it comes up while the image is not confirmed or the settings fell back (server/app/javascript/skyblip/README.md says how update.js reads it). 57 bytes for a release build at the widest versions scripts/build_image.sh lets through, 59 for a development build, and two more for a product other than skyblip_go, which names itself in product.

keys.name: image
keys.description: What became of the last install: confirmed, probation (running, not yet confirmed), reverted (started and never confirmed itself, so the bootloader swapped the old one back) or refused (never started)

keys.name: from
keys.description: The version the last install replaced, as dfu writes it, 0.3.0+1234. Present unless image is confirmed

keys.name: to
keys.description: The version the last install brought, as dfu writes it. Present unless image is confirmed

keys.name: settings
keys.description: What the settings in use fell back to at boot: prior, the copy written on the way into a swap, or defaults (products/skyblip_go/README.md). Absent when they loaded as stored

keys.name: swap_powered
keys.description: The cell allows the flash writes an install needs, by the settings write rule (core/power/cutoff.h)

keys.name: imu
keys.description: What the sensor hub's partition holds: none (no hub answered), missing, corrupt, unreadable (the external flash did not answer), writing (a full image is writing it now, up to a minute) or held

keys.name: imu_digest
keys.description: The first eight bytes of the verified hub blob's SHA-256, present when imu is held

keys.name: downgrade
keys.description: Present and true on a unit whose bootloader accepts an image older than the running one, a development build

keys.name: key
keys.description: The first four bytes of the hash of the signing key the bootloader trusts, as imgtool writes it in the image's KEYHASH TLV. Absent when the unit cannot read it

keys.name: product
keys.description: The product the unit runs, which is the only one whose images it installs (firmware/core/dfu/README.md), so a page offers it no other. Absent on a skyblip_go, so its frame stays as narrow as before the key, and on firmware built before the key, all of it skyblip_go

frames.description: Host to unit: asks to install the image of version, never in flight (in_flight) and with a cell that allows the swap (low_power). The unit answers confirm_dfu and asks on its glass, naming the version, and two presses answer dfu and open a ten-minute upload window for MCUmgr. A trusted browser (trust_browser) is not asked: the unit answers dfu and opens the window at once. The image that lands installs unasked, answered install, or refused nothing_staged, not_approved (not the version the presses authorised), wrong_key or low_power. A take-off does not close the window, and an image that lands in flight installs once the unit is back on the ground (server/app/javascript/skyblip/README.md). While a prompt stands it is refused prompt_pending, and after one press refused a prompt on this link refused_on_device, until the link drops (firmware/core/comms/README.md, One prompt at a time).

keys.name: version
keys.description: The image's version as read off its header, 0.2.0+15. Absent or unreadable is refused no_version, and older than the running image refused older unless the unit accepts a downgrade

frames.description: Host to unit: asks to enter the UF2 bootloader, never in flight (in_flight). The unit answers confirm_recovery and asks on its glass, and two presses answer recovery and hand the unit to the bootloader, a USB drive named TECHOBOOT (products/skyblip_go/README.md). While a prompt stands it is refused prompt_pending, and after one press refused a prompt on this link refused_on_device, until the link drops (firmware/core/comms/README.md, One prompt at a time).

Host to unit: asks to switch the unit off, never in flight (in_flight). The unit answers confirm_power_off and asks on its glass, and two presses answer power_off and start the shutdown. While a prompt stands it is refused prompt_pending, and after one press refused a prompt on this link refused_on_device, until the link drops (firmware/core/comms/README.md, One prompt at a time).

Opens an activation session (schemas/activation.v1.schema.json says what each signature covers). The host asks with the bare command, the unit draws a fresh Nu, which replaces any it held, and answers it with the id of the server key it trusts, so the server knows which of its keys to sign with: 27 bytes, answered small_mtu instead on a link that cannot carry it. The nonce dies when unlock uses it, when the link of the session that holds the claim drops, or after ten minutes. Refused keyless by a unit that has no key of its own, could not draw a nonce or cannot read its running version. A unit that lacks a required part, the barometer, shows its refusal page and does not advertise at all, so it cannot be activated. An activated unit refuses challenge, register and unlock as in_flight while it is airborne.

keys.name: nonce
keys.description: Nu, 16 random bytes from the hardware RNG, used once

keys.name: server_key_id
keys.description: The id of the server key the firmware is built to trust, the first four bytes of the SHA-256 of its raw 32-byte public key: every device build trusts skyblip.eu's server key (firmware/keys/server.pub), the host suite, the simulator and a local server the public test key of schemas/activation.v1.vectors.json

frames.description: Host to unit, 88 bytes. The unit checks R with the key it trusts and the nonce of this session, then asks on its glass under confirm_register. Two presses answer the registration frame, one press cancelled, thirty seconds expired. On a unit not yet activated the prompt stands whatever the flight state, because the unit is silent. An activated unit asks only when it is not airborne, and a take-off cancels the prompt. Refusals, in the order checked: prompt_pending (a prompt stands) and refused_on_device (one press refused a prompt on this link) (firmware/core/comms/README.md, One prompt at a time), in_flight (an activated unit in flight), keyless, no_session (no live nonce), small_mtu (the link cannot carry the registration frame in one notification), bad_signature.

keys.name: server_nonce
keys.description: Ns, the server's 16 random bytes, used once

keys.name: signature
keys.description: R, the server's Ed25519 signature over the register message, 'skyblip:register:v1' || Nu || Ns

frames.description: Unit to host after the two presses that answer register, at most 138 bytes in one notification, which an iPhone's 182-byte payload carries. The browser posts its keys to /activation/registrations as they are, byte strings in hexadecimal (schemas/activation.v1.schema.json).

keys.name: device_id
keys.description: DEVICEID, the eight bytes of FICR DEVICEID[1] then DEVICEID[0], each big-endian

keys.name: public_key
keys.description: Pd, the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key of the unit, whose seed comes from its key slot in UICR CUSTOMER (firmware/core/identity/README.md)

keys.name: version
keys.description: The running image's version as the dfu command writes it, 0.3.0+1234: at most 13 characters, 9.99.99+99999

keys.name: server_key_id
keys.description: The id of the server key the unit trusts, as in the challenge reply

keys.name: release
keys.description: The unit runs a release build, from a v* tag and the production image key, rather than a development build. Only told to the server, which keeps it beside the key: the air shows no difference, a development unit being a real aircraft with a real serial

keys.name: signature
keys.description: S, the unit's Ed25519 signature over the registration message (schemas/activation.v1.schema.json)

frames.description: Host to unit, at most 74 bytes, carrying what the server answered the registration with. The unit stores serial, Nu and U in its identity page only if U verifies with the key it trusts over its own DEVICEID, its current Pd, the serial and the nonce of this session, then answers acknowledgement with reason unlock and uses the serial from then on. Refused before the code is read, the nonce kept: in_flight (an activated unit in flight), no_session, low_power (the cell cannot take a flash write). Once read, the nonce is spent whether the code verifies or not: bad_signature (serial 0 included), flash (the identity page could not be written), or low_power if the cell fell while an activated unit placed the write.

keys.name: serial
keys.description: Assigned densely by the server, from 1 to 65535: serial 0 would put 0x000000 on the air, which decoders read as no address. The ADS-L address is the manufacturer prefix 0x00 followed by these 16 bits, under address mapping table 58

keys.name: signature
keys.description: U, the server's Ed25519 signature over the unlock message, 'skyblip:unlock:v1' || DEVICEID || Pd || serial as two bytes big-endian || Nu

frames.description: Host to unit on the log endpoint: without index, how many sessions the store holds, answered by a log frame, and with index, that session's entry, answered by a session frame (firmware/core/comms/README.md, The log dialect).

keys.name: log
keys.description: Which store the command addresses: flights, or diagnostics. Absent is flights, and a code that is neither is refused unknown_log

keys.name: index
keys.description: The entry to describe, from 0. Past the last one is refused no_session

frames.description: Host to unit on the log endpoint: asks for count chunks of session from record from, answered back to back by chunk frames. A chunk carries as many whole records as the asking link's payload holds, six at 182 bytes, nine at 244 and nineteen at 495. A link that cannot carry one record is answered small_mtu, and a session the store does not hold no_session.

keys.name: log
keys.description: Which store the command addresses: flights, or diagnostics. Absent is flights, and a code that is neither is refused unknown_log

keys.name: session
keys.description: The session to read, by its id as a session frame names it. A read without it is refused unknown_command

keys.name: from
keys.description: The record to start at, absent meaning 0

keys.name: count
keys.description: Chunks to send back to back, absent meaning 1, clamped to 1 to 8 (kMaxLogReadChunks)

frames.description: Host to unit on the log endpoint: asks to erase the flights store. The prompt and its verdict travel on the config endpoint: the unit answers confirm_erase_log and asks on its glass, and two presses answer erase_log. Once the store is erased the log endpoint answers a log frame with reason erased. The diagnostics store, which is recycled rather than erased, is refused flights_only, and an erase in flight in_flight. On the config endpoint, an erase is refused prompt_pending while a prompt stands, and refused_on_device after one press refused a prompt on this link, until the link drops (firmware/core/comms/README.md, One prompt at a time).

keys.name: log
keys.description: Which store the command addresses: flights, or diagnostics. Absent is flights, and a code that is neither is refused unknown_log

frames.description: Unit to host on the log endpoint: the answer to list without an index, the refusal of a log command, and erased once an erase the presses authorised completes.

keys.name: log
keys.description: The store this reply is about: diagnostics on every diagnostics reply, absent for flights, so two fetches on one link never misfile a chunk

keys.name: acknowledge
keys.description: The command was carried out. False is a refusal named by reason

keys.name: reason
keys.description: The refusal, or erased. Absent on the answer to list

keys.name: sessions
keys.description: How many sessions the store's index offers, on the answer to list

keys.name: truncated
keys.description: On the answer to list, the partition holds more sessions than the index offers

frames.description: Unit to host on the log endpoint: one entry of the store's index, the answer to list with an index. An entry of 256 records or more does not fit the 20 bytes of a link that never exchanged its MTU.

keys.name: log
keys.description: The store this reply is about: diagnostics on every diagnostics reply, absent for flights, so two fetches on one link never misfile a chunk

keys.name: index
keys.description: The entry this is, from 0

keys.name: of
keys.description: How many entries the index holds

keys.name: session
keys.description: The session's id, its opening UTC second: its name, and the base every one of its records is timed against

keys.name: records
keys.description: Records the session holds

keys.name: closed
keys.description: The session was closed. False means the log stops where the power did, and a reader says so rather than present a cut flight as whole

keys.name: truncated
keys.description: The session opened in a sector the ring recycled since, so what is left is a suffix renumbered from record 0, not the whole run

frames.description: Unit to host on the log endpoint: records of one session, an answer to read. Each chunk carries the index it starts at, so the next read is the acknowledgement and asking again from the last index kept is the whole recovery.

keys.name: log
keys.description: The store this reply is about: diagnostics on every diagnostics reply, absent for flights, so two fetches on one link never misfile a chunk

keys.name: session
keys.description: The session these records belong to

keys.name: from
keys.description: The index of the first record in records

keys.name: ends_session
keys.description: This chunk holds the session's last record, and no other chunk of a window says so

keys.name: records
keys.description: Whole records, 24 bytes each as the flash holds them, CRC and all, so the host checks each against the checksum the flash wrote. Their count is the length over 24

frames.description: Host to unit: asks for a cold start of the GNSS receiver, never in flight (in_flight). The unit answers confirm_gnss_cold_start and asks on its glass, and two presses answer gnss_cold_start and restart the receiver cold. While a prompt stands it is refused prompt_pending, and after one press refused a prompt on this link refused_on_device, until the link drops (firmware/core/comms/README.md, One prompt at a time).

Host to unit, proposed: a drawing of the own-ship symbol for one aircraft type, which the ownship editor shows (server/content/ownships/README.md). No firmware reads it yet, so a unit answers unknown_command.

keys.name: aircraft_type
keys.description: The ADS-L aircraft category the drawing is for

keys.name: width
keys.description: The drawing's width in columns, 3 to 32

keys.name: hot_spot
keys.description: The row the aircraft's position is drawn on

keys.name: rows
keys.description: The drawing, one 32-bit word per row and 1 to 32 rows, big-endian, the leftmost column in the lowest bit, so its length over 4 is the number of rows

frames.description: Bravo to its paired Go on the peer endpoint: one ADS-B target as Bravo's model::AircraftObservation holds it (firmware/core/model/README.md), at most two frames a second for each target, what Bravo hears in between folded into the next. Each field carries its own validity and time: a key with no valid reading behind it is absent, and each age counts back from at_s and into_ms as the observation's ages count back from at_ms. A frame is never sent again with a fresher time: a field not heard again keeps its instant, and its age is rebased whenever the observation's reference instant moves, so forwarding never refreshes a target. RSSI is not carried. 126 bytes at its widest, the widest peer frame, so 126 is the payload a pairing needs (firmware/core/comms/README.md, The peer endpoint).

keys.name: address
keys.description: The target's 24-bit ICAO address, from its DF17 message. Bravo decodes DF17 alone, so the address is always an ICAO one, address mapping table 5, and the frame does not name its table

keys.name: boot_epoch
keys.description: Bravo's boot epoch: 32 bits Bravo draws from its hardware random number generator at boot and keeps until it restarts. A new value says Bravo restarted, so its sequence began again. Two boots draw the same value once in 2^32

keys.name: sequence
keys.description: This frame's number among the observations Bravo sent since boot, every target counted together: 0 for the first, one more for each frame after, and 0 again after 4294967295. A reader orders two numbers of one boot_epoch by serial number arithmetic (RFC 1982, SERIAL_BITS 32): a is newer than b when (a - b) mod 2^32 lies from 1 to 2^31 - 1. At 100 frames a second it wraps after 16 months

keys.name: at_s
keys.description: The UTC second, counted from 1970, of the instant the observation's at_ms names: the position's, or with no valid position the newest message's (firmware/core/model/README.md). Bravo sends nothing without UTC (#192)

keys.name: into_ms
keys.description: Milliseconds into at_s, 0 to 999, as events::Stamp counts them. Absent while Bravo's PPS phase is not valid, so the instant is known to the second only

keys.name: latitude_1e7
keys.description: The position's latitude in 1e-7 degrees, north positive, -900000000 to 900000000, as latitude_1e7. Present with longitude_1e7 while position_valid, and both absent otherwise, half a CPR pair included. Its time is at_s and into_ms. A Go refuses the frame for a value out of range

keys.name: longitude_1e7
keys.description: The position's longitude in 1e-7 degrees, east positive, -1800000000 to 1800000000, as longitude_1e7. Present with latitude_1e7. A Go refuses the frame for a value out of range

keys.name: altitude_m
keys.description: The target's GNSS height in whole metres above the WGS-84 ellipsoid, as altitude_m, measured or derived from the pressure altitude (firmware/core/model/README.md). Present while altitude_valid, -1318 to 39572: the pressure altitudes ADS-B encodes widened by the widest GNSS-baro difference it carries unsaturated, 3125 ft. A Go refuses the frame for a height outside it. Whether ADS-B's GNSS height is on that datum is settled with flight data (#183)

keys.name: altitude_age_ms
keys.description: How many milliseconds before at_s and into_ms altitude_m was true, negative when after, as altitude_age_ms. Present with altitude_m

keys.name: pressure_altitude_ft
keys.description: The target's pressure altitude on 1013.25 hPa in feet, as ADS-B encodes it and pressure_altitude_ft holds it, -1200 to 126700, the extremes of its Gillham code. Present while pressure_altitude_valid. A Go refuses the frame for a value outside it

keys.name: pressure_altitude_age_ms
keys.description: The age of pressure_altitude_ft, as pressure_altitude_age_ms. Present with it

keys.name: speed_q
keys.description: Ground speed in quarters of a metre a second, 0 to 65535, as speed_q. Present with track_c9 while speed_valid

keys.name: track_c9
keys.description: Track over the ground, 0 to 511, 360 degrees over 512 counts, as track_c9. Present with speed_q

keys.name: speed_age_ms
keys.description: The age of speed_q and track_c9, as speed_age_ms. Present with them

keys.name: climb_e8
keys.description: Vertical rate in eighths of a metre a second, up positive, -32768 to 32767, as climb_e8. Present while climb_valid

keys.name: climb_source
keys.description: What measured climb_e8, as climb_source: gnss or barometric, from the velocity message's VrSrc bit, and unknown when the source does not say. Present with climb_e8

keys.name: climb_age_ms
keys.description: The age of climb_e8, as climb_age_ms. Present with it

keys.name: flight_state
keys.description: ground or airborne, the target's flight state as flight_state holds it. Absent while it is unknown, so unknown never travels

keys.name: flight_state_age_ms
keys.description: The age of flight_state, as flight_state_age_ms. Present with it

keys.name: aircraft_category
keys.description: The ADS-L G.1.3 aircraft category protocol::adsb_emitter_to_adsl_category maps the target's emitter category into (firmware/core/protocol/README.md), as aircraft_category. Absent while it is 0, no category

keys.name: adsb_version
keys.description: The ADS-B version a type code 31 message names, 0 to 7, as adsb_version. Present once one was heard: until then the version is unknown, not 0

keys.name: gva
keys.description: The geometric vertical accuracy code, 0 to 3, as gva. Present once an airborne type code 31 from a version 2 transmitter was heard

keys.name: callsign
keys.description: The target's identification, at most eight characters as ADS-B's identification message carries them, trailing blanks removed, as Bravo's traffic::CallsignTable holds it for the address. Absent while the table holds none. Dated by callsign_heard_s alone: it never moves at_s or an age, so a callsign heard alone never refreshes the position

keys.name: callsign_heard_s
keys.description: The UTC second Bravo last heard callsign, as traffic::CallsignTable dates it. Absent, while callsign is present, when the table dated it before Bravo held UTC: bus::State::traffic_now_s() falls back to seconds of uptime then

frames.description: Bravo to its paired Go on the peer endpoint, once a second whatever the traffic, so the Go tells an empty sky from a lost link (#193). It says which position Bravo places its exports against, and whether Bravo keeps its alarm silent for this Go (#179), and the transponder it takes for the aircraft's own. 48 bytes at its widest. Keys 8 to 10 are retired (#179) and never reused.

keys.name: protocol_version
keys.description: The version of the peer frames Bravo speaks: 1, observation, health and peer_claim as this registry gives them. It moves when a peer key changes meaning, not when one is added

keys.name: boot_epoch
keys.description: Bravo's boot epoch, the one its observations carry

keys.name: listening
keys.description: Bravo's 1090 MHz receiver is armed. False before it is and after a fault takes it down, so the Go can tell a deaf receiver from a lost link (#193)

keys.name: utc_valid
keys.description: Bravo holds UTC from its own receiver. Without it Bravo sends no observation, and exports nothing to an EFB either (#192)

keys.name: last_sequence
keys.description: The sequence of the last observation Bravo sent in this boot_epoch. Absent before the first

keys.name: own_icao_set
keys.description: Bravo's own-ICAO setting holds an address, so the aircraft's own transponder is not traffic even when the Go sends no own_icao (#184)

keys.name: alarm_granted
keys.description: Bravo keeps its buzzer and haptic silent for this Go (#179): true exactly while this is the Go Bravo pinned, its connection is up, and its last peer_claim said alarm_requested true and is younger than three claim periods. False is Bravo sounding by its own alarm_enabled and alarm_volume. Bravo's NMEA stream to an EFB is unchanged either way

keys.name: export_reference
keys.description: The position Bravo places its exports against, to the Go and to an EFB (#192): go, the Go's from a fresh peer_claim, own, Bravo's own valid fix, or none, so Bravo exports nothing. Bravo reports the reference it would use, whatever utc_valid says, and exports only while this is not none and utc_valid is true

keys.name: paired
keys.description: Bravo holds this Go's pin, or offers it since its button answered this Go's request (#192). A Go asking to pair pins Bravo only on true. A paired Go that reads false holds a pin Bravo does not, from a pairing cut short or a Bravo that pinned another Go, so it drops its pin and says so

keys.name: own_transponder
keys.description: The 24-bit ICAO address of the transponder Bravo takes for the aircraft's own: the loudest DF17 emitter it hears, above a floor and ahead of every other one by a lead, for a hold (products/skyblip_bravo/README.md, Own transponder). Bravo hears it before its own-ICAO filter, so it stays present once the address is set. Never 0, which as own_icao means unset, and a Go refuses a health that carries 0. Absent while no emitter qualifies. The Go proposes it as own_icao only on the ground and only on the pilot's press

keys.name: own_transponder_callsign
keys.description: own_transponder's identification, at most eight characters as ADS-B's identification message carries them, trailing blanks removed. Absent without own_transponder, and until its identification is heard

keys.name: own_transponder_category
keys.description: The ADS-L G.1.3 aircraft category protocol::adsb_emitter_to_adsl_category maps own_transponder's emitter category into, as observation's aircraft_category. Absent without own_transponder, and while it is 0, no category

frames.description: The Go to Bravo on the peer endpoint, once a second while it pairs and while paired: the Go's own-ship, its own ICAO, whether it takes the alarm (#179), and whether it holds Bravo's pin. Bravo takes the own-ship, the own ICAO and the request only from the Go it pinned, and reads paired from any Go (#192). Its ages count back from the instant the Go wrote the frame, so they hold whether or not the Go has UTC, and UTC never stands for a position: each field is valid on its own. 72 bytes at its widest. Keys 13 to 17 are retired (#179) and never reused.

keys.name: boot_epoch
keys.description: The Go's boot epoch, drawn as Bravo's is (observation's boot_epoch)

keys.name: at_s
keys.description: The UTC second, counted from 1970, at which the Go wrote this frame. Absent while the Go holds no UTC

keys.name: into_ms
keys.description: Milliseconds into at_s, 0 to 999, as events::Stamp counts them. Absent without at_s, and while the Go's PPS phase is not valid

keys.name: latitude_1e7
keys.description: The Go's latitude in 1e-7 degrees, north positive, own-ship's latitude_1e7. Present with longitude_1e7 and position_age_ms while own-ship's fix_valid

keys.name: longitude_1e7
keys.description: The Go's longitude in 1e-7 degrees, east positive, own-ship's longitude_1e7. Present with latitude_1e7

keys.name: position_age_ms
keys.description: Milliseconds from own-ship's fix_at_ms, the fix the position came from, to the instant the Go wrote this frame. Present with latitude_1e7

keys.name: altitude_hae_mm
keys.description: The Go's height above the WGS-84 ellipsoid in millimetres, own-ship's altitude_hae_mm, which an ADS-B target's GNSS height is compared with. Present while own-ship's fix_valid, since model::Ownship gives it no validity of its own

keys.name: altitude_hae_age_ms
keys.description: Milliseconds from the fix altitude_hae_mm came from to the instant the Go wrote this frame. Equal to position_age_ms until model::Ownship dates the height apart from the position. Present with altitude_hae_mm

keys.name: pressure_altitude_mm
keys.description: The Go's pressure altitude on 1013.25 hPa in millimetres, own-ship's pressure_altitude_mm, which a target that sends no GNSS height is compared with. Present while own-ship's pressure_altitude_valid

keys.name: pressure_altitude_age_ms
keys.description: Milliseconds from own-ship's pressure_altitude_at_ms to the instant the Go wrote this frame. Present with pressure_altitude_mm

keys.name: own_icao
keys.description: The Go's own-ICAO setting, the 24-bit address of the aircraft's own transponder (#191). Present when set

keys.name: alarm_requested
keys.description: The Go takes the alarm for the pair, so Bravo keeps its buzzer and haptic silent (#179). True only while the Go has a buzzer or a haptic, a valid fix, Bravo's pin and a Bravo it reads live, whatever its own alarm_enabled and alarm_volume say, so off on the Go keeps the pair silent. A Go with neither part never takes it. Bravo heeds it only from the Go it pinned, while that Go's connection is up and for three claim periods after the claim, and sounds by its own settings again after a claim with false, a disconnect or an unpair

keys.name: paired
keys.description: The Go holds this Bravo's pin: true from the health that pinned it, false while the Go asks to pair. A claim with paired false is the Go's pairing request, and Bravo stores its own pin only once it reads true from the Go its press answered, and health's paired tells a Go when Bravo holds none, so neither side keeps a pin alone (#192). A Go that unpairs while connected writes one claim with false, so Bravo drops its pin too

frames.description: Host to unit: asks to arm a diagnostics capture under profile, or to stop the one running (#247). Only a skyBlip Bravo answers it, because it has no glass to arm one on. A Go answers unknown_command and arms a capture on its glass only (firmware/products/skyblip_go/README.md, Which capture is armed). Refused, in the order checked: prompt_pending while a prompt stands and refused_on_device after one press refused a prompt on this link (firmware/core/comms/README.md, One prompt at a time), in_flight while the unit is airborne, invalid without a profile, out_of_range for a profile past stop, no_storage on a unit whose flash holds no capture ring, capturing for an arm while a capture runs, and not_capturing for a stop while none runs. Otherwise the unit answers confirm_capture and blinks the prompt on its lamp, and two presses answer capture and arm the profile or stop the capture. A take-off cancels the prompt. 6 bytes at its widest.

keys.name: profile
keys.description: full, power_run or flight_run arms a capture of that profile (firmware/core/diagnostics/README.md), and stop stops the capture that runs

frames.description: Opens a trusted-browser session (firmware/core/comms/README.md, Trusted browsers). The host asks with the bare command, the unit draws a fresh nonce for the session that holds the claim, which replaces any it held, and answers it: 22 bytes, answered small_mtu instead on a link that cannot carry it. The nonce dies when trust_browser uses it or when the link of the session that holds the claim drops, and a new browser_challenge also ends the trust a trusted session held until trust_browser proves a key again. Refused keyless by a unit that cannot draw a nonce. Answered in flight as on the ground.

keys.name: nonce
keys.description: 16 random bytes from the hardware RNG, used once

frames.description: Host to unit, at most 133 bytes: the browser's public key, signed over the nonce of browser_challenge. The nonce is spent before the check. Refused no_session without a live nonce for this claim holder, invalid for a label wider than 24 bytes and bad_signature when the signature does not verify with key. A key the unit trusts answers acknowledgement true with reason trusted, and the session stays trusted until its link drops: a set is stored without a prompt, in flight too, and a dfu opens the upload window without a prompt. Any other key answers acknowledgement false with reason untrusted, and the unit holds it with its label for this session: the next set or dfu that two presses confirm on this link stores it among the trusted browsers. The unit keeps eight, and a ninth replaces the one stored first. Answered in flight as on the ground.

keys.name: key
keys.description: The browser's raw Ed25519 public key, from a key pair it generated and cannot export (server/app/javascript/skyblip/README.md, Trusted browsers)

keys.name: signature
keys.description: The browser's Ed25519 signature over 'skyblip:browser:v1' || the nonce of browser_challenge

keys.name: label
keys.description: What the browser calls itself in the list of trusted browsers, such as 'Chrome on Android', at most 24 bytes of UTF-8. Absent is an empty label

frames.description: Host to unit: asks for one entry of the unit's trusted browsers, which it answers with browser. Answered only to a trusted session (trust_browser), refused untrusted otherwise. A page asks from index 0 until browser says the index is past the last entry.

keys.name: index
keys.description: Which entry, from 0, in the order the unit stored them

frames.description: Unit to host, the answer to browsers: the entry at index, or index and count alone past the last entry. 45 bytes at its widest.

keys.name: index
keys.description: The index browsers asked for

keys.name: count
keys.description: How many browsers the unit trusts, 0 to 8

keys.name: id
keys.description: The first eight bytes of the browser's public key, which names it to forget_browser and lets a browser find itself in the list. Absent past the last entry

keys.name: label
keys.description: The label the browser sent with its key, possibly empty. Absent past the last entry

frames.description: Host to unit, 14 bytes: drops the browser id names from the trusted browsers. Answered only to a trusted session, refused untrusted otherwise. The unit answers acknowledgement true with reason forgotten, or false with reason unknown_browser when it trusts no browser by that id. A session that forgets its own browser is no longer trusted. Answered in flight as on the ground.

keys.name: id
keys.description: The browser to forget, as browser names it

frames.description: Temporary: #293 removes it once the trial picks the LR2021's settings. Host to unit, 64 bytes at its widest: runs a reception trial on a skyBlip Bravo's 1090 MHz receiver, or stops the one running (firmware/products/skyblip_bravo/services/adsb_trial.md). Only a development Bravo answers it, and every other image answers unknown_command. thresholds_dbm holds one entry per profile, and each other array, when present, holds one entry per profile too. A frame with no key but the command stops the trial and puts the receiver back on its default tuning. Refused invalid for a key of the wrong type, an empty thresholds_dbm, an array whose length differs from thresholds_dbm's, thresholds_dbm without slot_s, or another key without thresholds_dbm, and out_of_range for more than eight profiles or a value past its range. Otherwise answered acknowledgement true with reason adsb_trial, at once and with no prompt, in flight as on the ground. The trial lives in RAM, so a restart ends it.

keys.name: slot_s
keys.description: How long each profile listens before the next takes over, 5 to 255 s. Required with thresholds_dbm

keys.name: thresholds_dbm
keys.description: Each profile's OOK detection threshold in dBm below zero, 90 for -90 dBm, 11 to 128. The unit writes the threshold plus 74 into register 0xF30E14, as Semtech's driver does (firmware/hardware/parts/lr2021/README.md)

keys.name: gain_steps
keys.description: Each profile's SetAgcGainManual step: 0 runs the AGC, and 1 to 13 fix the gain. All 0 when absent

keys.name: boosts
keys.description: Each profile's LF path boost in SetRxPath, 0 to 7. All 0 when absent

keys.name: front_ends
keys.description: Each profile's write into register 0xF30150: 1 writes 0x18, SoftRF's, which stops the AGC and the blanking of a saturated ADC, and 0 writes 0x75, the part's own. All 1 when absent

keys.name: layouts
keys.description: Each profile's frame layout: 0 is 27 bytes of raw chips behind the 0x95 sync word, SoftRF's, and 1 is the part's inverted Manchester decoding of 14 bytes with no sync word, cb-tfc's. All 0 when absent
